title: Slack API Guide: Access, Rate Limits, Errors (2026)
summary: Slack API has four entry points, each with different rate limits and errors. Determine which one you need and what constraints to expect.
body_markdown:
## Calling Slack Endpoints Without Code in Activepieces


Slack is one of the 750 integrations Activepieces counts from its MIT-licensed open source monorepo, every connected integration is available to the AI as a tool with its credentials held centrally, and a Slack method the integration doesn't cover can be generated with AI and added privately to your own instance.


That means you can start with a running flow and read Slack's responses in the run trace, rather than writing the retry and queueing code the previous section described before anything runs.


You don't hire for this, you describe it: tell the built-in chat what should reach which channel, and what it publishes is a live flow in your account, open to read step by step, the same artifact a builder would have assembled by hand.


The flow then runs under the platform's RBAC and audit logs like any other, and its run trace shows exactly what happened on each run, naming the failing step and Slack's response, whether that's a ratelimited 429 or a missing_scope, so whoever's paged at 2am can read it without knowing Slack's internals.


### Using the Slack connector


The connector wraps common actions such as sending a message to a channel, and it has triggers for new messages and similar events. You authenticate once, pick the action, and fill in the fields.


In the flow below, a Stripe "Payment Failed" trigger is paired with a "Send Message To A Channel" action. The right panel shows the action's authentication, channel and message template, and the left sidebar shows step_1 completed in 574ms under a "Run succeeded" banner.


What to take from it: the whole process is two steps. The run details record the outcome of each step, so a failed delivery or a rejected call appears there when it happens rather than after a user reports it.


The connector exposes a chosen set of methods, not the whole Slack API, and because the 750 integrations are counted from the open source monorepo, you can read the Slack integration's source to see exactly which actions and triggers it offers before you rely on them.


### Calling Other Slack API Methods via HTTP


When the connector lacks a method you need, the HTTP step sends a request to the Slack Web API endpoint directly, using your app's token in the authorization header.


You must then confirm that token carries the scopes that method requires, since Slack enforces them regardless of the tool calling it.


When a scope is missing or Slack rate-limits a call, the response comes back in the run trace, which tells you what to fix.


Some work stays in code. A custom app built on Socket Mode needs a persistent connection that a flow doesn't hold open.


Large history exports mean paging through many pages of results under Slack's per-method limits, and that's better served by a purpose-built script you control and can schedule.
